findings.evidence: `multipoleS_fin_one` (Multipole.lean:105) proves `multipoleS U x y = dipoleS U (x 0) (y 0)`, so the dipole is literally the n = 1 member; `public import EpsilonEridani.QFT.SmallX.Dipole.Operator` (Multipole.lean:8) makes the specialisation unavailable in the direction it is needed. Checking the reversal claim: `(∏ᵢ U(xᵢ)U(yᵢ)†)† = ∏ⱼ U(y_{n-1-j})U(x_{n-1-j})†`, which is `multipoleS U (y ∘ Fin.rev) (x ∘ Fin.rev)`; at n = 2 this is `quadrupoleS U w z y x` and at n = 1 it is `dipoleS U y x`, i.e. exactly the two lemmas as stated.
findings.fix: Put `multipoleS` upstream of `dipoleS` (define it in `Operator.lean` or a module it imports), set `dipoleS U x y := multipoleS U ![x] ![y]` alongside `quadrupoleS U x y z w := multipoleS U ![x, z] ![y, w]`, and prove each property once at `multipoleS`: `multipoleS_self`; reversal `multipoleS U x y = multipoleS U (y ∘ Fin.rev) (x ∘ Fin.rev)` (the product's `star` reverses the list), which gives `dipoleS_comm` at n = 1 and `quadrupoleS_reverse` at n = 2; gauge invariance under `∀ i, Ωm (x i) = Ωm (y i)` and `∀ i, Ωp (y i) = Ωp (x (i + 1))`, which gives both `dipoleS_gaugeTransform` and `quadrupoleS_gaugeTransform`.
findings.issue: `multipoleS` is defined in a module that imports `Dipole/Operator.lean`, i.e. downstream of its own `n = 1` case, so the general results cannot specialise to the dipole and three facts are proved twice: `multipoleS_self` (:99) vs `dipoleS_self` (Operator.lean:73); `quadrupoleS_reverse` (:179) vs `dipoleS_comm` (Operator.lean:78) — the PR rewrites the latter into exactly the same `conjTranspose` + `re_trace_conjTranspose` shape; `quadrupoleS_gaugeTransform` (:192) vs `dipoleS_gaugeTransform` (Operator.lean:103), the same telescoping `key` plus `trace_unitary_conj`.

findings.evidence: Multipole.lean:144 proves it by `trace_mul_comm` on the two-factor split — the identical argument splits `List.ofFn f` as head/tail for any n; no general statement exists in the file (grep for `multipoleS_` yields only `_def`, `_self`, `_fin_one`, `_fin_two`, `abs_`).
findings.fix: State the single-step rotation at the general level, `multipoleS U x y = multipoleS U (x ∘ (· + 1)) (y ∘ (· + 1))` for `x y : Fin (n+1) → _`, via `List.ofFn_succ` and `Matrix.trace_mul_comm`, and obtain `quadrupoleS_cycle` as the n = 2 instance (it is then also what `quadrupoleS_self_right` and `_self_outer` are derived from, unchanged).
findings.issue: `quadrupoleS_cycle` states cyclic invariance only at n = 2, but it is `trace_mul_comm` applied to the whole product and holds for `multipoleS` at every n. Roadmap Layer 5.3 consumes the general correlator ('the n-th equation involves the (n+1)-st correlator'), so a consumer at n ≥ 3 has no cyclicity lemma and must redo the trace argument. The module docstring (:40-42) already advertises the cancellation and shift mechanism as general.

summary: The general correlator is defined downstream of its own n = 1 case, so the reversal, gauge-invariance and transparency results are each proved twice (dipole and quadrupole) instead of once at `multipoleS`; cyclicity is likewise stated only at n = 2 although it is a property of the trace at every n.
